top_choice_rationale: P003 (Chetty, Hendren, Friedman) is the clearest case of measurement and causal identification done together. Linked population records make mobility a measurable, place-specific quantity, and the movers and exposure-effect designs test whether place causes outcomes. The descriptive and causal strands constrain each other, and the work has changed research in public, labour and urban economics. Friedman fits a citation about administrative-data measurement better than Katz, whose Moving to Opportunity and wage-structure work fits P001. The main discount is maturity: the results date from about 2014, long-run robustness is still being tested, and restricted data limit independent re-analysis. I count that as real and have not verified how closely register studies elsewhere agree. P001, limited to the trade and technology exposure evidence with Dorn as third name, is a close second. It has the longer replication record, but magnitudes and shift-share identification remain debated. P002 is mature and well attributed, but its empirical bite is indirect. P005 has looser attribution, because Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, and its welfare estimates depend on specification. P004 has the thinnest empirical support for the lobbying mechanism. All five ranked proposals are preferred to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. No co-author or network named in my profile is credited on P001 to P005. My profile lists a co-author named Persson on a corruption paper, without a first name, and I make no claim about identity; Torsten Persson appears only on B027, which is not in the slate. I work on measurement and causal inference, so I may be inclined toward P003 and P001, and I treat that as field familiarity rather than evidence of merit. I gave the 2024 presentation speech, which reflects Academy drafting and shows no preference among 2026 candidates. Hassler, Krusell and Boppart are Stockholm University colleagues in a different department. No conflict is adjudicated.
